newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth COO sets long-distance goal.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth COO sets long-distance goal.

text.p: BellSouth Corp Chief Operating Officer F. Duane Ackerman, who takes over the corporate helm in January, said on Thursday that the regional company will be ready to enter the long-distance market by mid-1997.

"We're preparing out business to be in long distance by the middle of next year. Whether (actual competition with long distance carriers) is the middle of next year or a month or two later, I don't think there's any way to discern that. But we are going to be prepared," he told reporters at a press luncheon.
Meanwhile, at a time when consolidation is sweeping other regional Bell holding companies, Ackerman said BellSouth has yet to find a prospective merger parter which offers adequate value.

"We have spent a lot of time looking, obviously, at some of the horizontal mergers that have gone on and been going on, and so far we haven't had a hit that we felt like was right for us from a value point of view," he expalined.
Ackerman, who also serves as BellSouth vice-chairman, will become chief executive in January after current CEO John Clendenin retires.
He said a merger for the sake of gaining scale was precluded by the sheer size of BellSouth's current operations, which span 25 million customers worldwide.
"It's very difficult for us to identify a merger that creates more additional value, than perhaps it would provide a distraction as it relates to padding down a very large merger, Ackerman said.

Ackerman said BellSouth is preparing for what it considers an inevitable price war against AT&T Corp and other potential long-distance rivals by beefing up its marketing and advertising initiatives throughout the Southeast.
